note: Narration and the user's spoken lines are synthetic speech (Microsoft neural voices). The user lines are fed to the emulator's microphone and go through the real Whisper + Llama path on our Worker.

scenes.say: The end of the day, and your head is still full of loose ends. Loose Ends is a five-minute wind-down for Quest. Say what's on your mind, then sort it. Every action works three ways: a pinch, your voice, or just looking.
I look at the orb to start listening, and just talk.
scenes.user: Um, okay. I need to email Priya about the budget by Friday. And book the car in for its service tomorrow. Oh, and the leaky kitchen tap, honestly, let it go.

scenes.say: Whisper turns the ramble into text, and Llama splits it into clean cards. It only keeps a card if I actually said those words, so nothing gets invented.
Where it can tell from what I said, Llama also suggests a tray, written under the card. It never sorts on its own. If I agree, I just say so.
One step for all of them, and one Undo puts them all back. Tonight I'd rather sort them myself.
Hands first: reach out, pinch a card, and drop it on a tray.
Or no hands at all. Look at a card until the ring fills, then look at a tray.

scenes.user: Fix the bike light, let it go.

scenes.say: Settings work the same way. Bigger text and high contrast are one phrase away.
When I'm done, it reads back tomorrow's plan, and a plant on the desk grows a leaf for every evening I close out.
Loose Ends. Built with Meta's Immersive Web SDK, it runs in the Quest browser with nothing to install. Five quiet minutes, then sleep.
